transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessett says it's too soon to say whether
former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Wong should return to his leadership role.
He says it depends on the outcome of an investigation into who sold
advanced computer chips to China and if it complied with U.S. export restrictions.
NPR's Shonda Lee Stuster reports.
Bessett says NVIDIA has not answered questions about compliance after his
previous demand to do so within 10 days.
On CBS News' Face the Nation, Bessett said the Treasury Department has been
in touch with the company's temporary management and lawyers.
It behooves NVIDIA to move quickly on this because we want to know what the
culture was. Was there a promiscuous attitude toward this?
And if it happened, where were the faults? And then they can move on.
Bessett had previously said there was a, quote, "culture of non-compliance"
at the company. On Sunday, he said it's a possibility and that the board is
moving quickly to determine if that exists.
Shonda Lee Stuster, NPR News.
European Union negotiators say they're deeply disappointed with the collapse
of climate talks in Turkey.
NPR's Terry Schultz reports the EU team said it could not accept the final draft
that admitted the mention of fossil fuel.
Despite record-long and extended negotiations to reach a compromise,
Irish Environment Minister Dara O'Brien, negotiating on behalf of the EU,
said the absence of any mention of transitioning away from coal, oil,
and gas was a disgrace.
We could not, with any good conscience, support a text that effectively denies
what is happening in the world and was hijacked by fossil fuel producers.
O'Brien's fellow negotiator, EU Climate Commissioner Wobke Hoekstra,
echoed the disappointment.
This is larger than just all of us. This is something that doesn't discriminate
and that humanity urgently needs to tackle.
Hoekstra said the EU will continue working with like-minded countries
and redouble its own efforts to combat climate change.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
♪♪
Authorities in Indonesia say it's too early to determine how many people died
through a candle factory in near the capital of Jakarta.
At least 24 people are dead, but the death toll could go higher
as crews are searching for 34 workers who are still considered missing.
Families of young children say they are kind if the families are kind,
even as they see the world overwhelmingly as an unkind place.
This, according to a new survey now from the Sesame Workshop.
NPR's Corey Turner reports.
The education nonprofit behind Sesame Street has twice surveyed American families
about kindness in 2016 and now a decade later.
And the differences are striking.
This national sample of caregivers of kids ages 3 to 8 saw a big increase
in families who say kindness is just not a priority for most people.
And they gave Americans a pretty middling rating for kindness, 2.8 out of 5.
But compared to a decade ago, kids earned higher marks for kindness and resilience,
and they were less likely to be considered anxious.
Caregivers themselves were also much more likely in 2026 to say they value empathy
in their kids over manners.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
For the first time since 2021, the Big Ten conference does not have a football team
in the top five of the AP top 25 rankings.
In fact, the Big Ten team's UCLA is number ten, a drop of six positions,
and Indiana also is out of the top ten.
Georgia is number one.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Treasury Secretary Bessett says Jensen Wong's NVIDIA return depends on chip-export investigation
EU negotiators condemn collapse of Turkey climate talks over missing fossil fuel language
Indonesia candle factory fire kills at least 24, with 34 workers still missing
Sesame Workshop survey finds caregivers see less kindness in Americans than a decade ago
Big Ten has no team in AP top five for first time since 2021; UCLA falls to tenth
